root_cause.text: The GCS page table macros `_PAGE_GCS` and `_PAGE_GCS_RO` unconditionally set `PTE_SHARED` bits (bits 8-9), which when FEAT_LPA2 is enabled are repurposed as high-order physical address bits (50-51), causing corrupted page table entries and translation faults.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The GCS page protection macros _PAGE_GCS and _PAGE_GCS_RO include the PTE_SHARED bits (0b11), but on systems with FEAT_LPA2 these bits are repurposed as physical address bits 50–51, causing invalid page table entries and a translation fault when LPA2 is enabled, because the code did not clear PTE_SHARED for GCS mappings as it does for the regular protection_map.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused PAGE_GCS and PAGE_GCS_RO macro definitions to clean up the header.
intent_record.what: Removed the macro definitions PAGE_GCS and PAGE_GCS_RO, which were defined as __pgprot wrappers around _PAGE_GCS and _PAGE_GCS_RO.
intent_record.how: These macros are no longer available for use elsewhere in the kernel, which will cause a compile error if any code references them. Any existing use must have been removed or replaced prior to this change.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a static read-only-after-init variable for GCS page protection to support future Guarded Control Stack functionality.
intent_record.what: Added a static variable `gcs_page_prot` of type `ptdesc_t` initialized to `_PAGE_GCS_RO` and marked `__ro_after_init` after the `protection_map` array definition.
intent_record.how: Introduces a new per-architecture page protection descriptor for Guarded Control Stack (GCS) pages, which can be set during early boot and remains read-only afterwards, providing a consistent protection flag for GCS mappings.

intent_record.intent_summary: When LPA2 is enabled, also clear the PTE_SHARED bit in gcs_page_prot to match the existing adjustment made to protection_map, fixing an incomplete initialization.
intent_record.what: Added clearing of the PTE_SHARED bit from gcs_page_prot inside the if (lpa2_is_enabled()) block, which previously only cleared it from protection_map entries.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when lpa2_is_enabled() returns true, the code now additionally clears the PTE_SHARED bit from gcs_page_prot, ensuring consistent page protection attributes for GCS pages.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace hardcoded `_PAGE_GCS_RO` with `gcs_page_prot` to use the correct dynamic page protection for shadow stack pages in GCS (Guarded Control Stack) feature.
intent_record.what: Replaced the hardcoded constant `_PAGE_GCS_RO` with the variable `gcs_page_prot` in the assignment of `prot` when setting page protection for shadow stack pages under GCS.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the page protection for shadow stack pages is now determined by the value of `gcs_page_prot` instead of a fixed constant, allowing the protection to be dynamically chosen based on system configuration or other conditions.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure correct GCS page protection by using the dynamically initialized gcs_page_prot that accounts for LPA2 adjustments.

relevance_review.reason: The group removes the PAGE_GCS and PAGE_GCS_RO macros, which are the direct cause of the vulnerability as they set PTE_SHARED bits that corrupt page table entries when FEAT_LPA2 is enabled.

The group adds a static variable for future GCS page protection, which does not directly address or relate to the vulnerability caused by macros unconditionally setting PTE_SHARED bits when FEAT_LPA2 is enabled.

The group directly addresses the root cause by adjusting gcs_page_prot to clear PTE_SHARED when LPA2 is enabled and using the corrected dynamic protection instead of the hardcoded _PAGE_GCS_RO macro that unconditionally set those bits.

Same root cause as _PAGE_GCS: includes _PAGE_DEFAULT which unconditionally sets PTE_SHARED bits, leading to corruption when LPA2 repurposes those bits for high-order physical addresses.
